Here is the revised, visual-first creative proposal for the interactive scroll-driven exploded gearbox sequence, updated strictly to reflect your technical framing, vector constraints, and closed-form progress requirements without generating code or altering approved mechanics.

---

### Core Technical & Cinematography Framework

#### 1. Closed-Form Parametric Sampling
To guarantee deterministic behavior across forward, reverse, and arbitrary jump seeks, camera position \\(\mathbf{P}(t)\\) and look-at target \\(\mathbf{T}(t)\\) are defined strictly as **pure closed-form functions of progress** \\(t = \text{animationPhase} \in [1]\\) [2-7]. Frame-history-dependent state updates (such as frame-to-frame LERP or exponential damping) are omitted from production seek logic to avoid frame-rate dependence, lag, or path hysteresis. Evaluating at any progress value \\(t\\) yields instantaneous, identical 3D camera and component transforms [6, 7].

#### 2. Vector & Angle Bounds (\\(\text{abs}(\mathbf{v}_{\text{view}} \cdot \mathbf{v}_{\text{motion}}) < 0.6\\))
To enforce an elevated side three-quarter perspective and strictly prevent near-boresight "down-the-shaft" views during axial translations, the camera line-of-sight vector \\(\mathbf{v}_{\text{view}}\\) and motion axis vector \\(\mathbf{v}_{\text{motion}}\\) must satisfy:
\\[\text{abs}(\mathbf{v}_{\text{view}} \cdot \mathbf{v}_{\text{motion}}) < 0.6\\]
This maintains an angle of at least \\(\approx 53.1^\circ\\) between the camera's optical axis and the mechanical explosion axis throughout all translation moves.

#### 3. Preserved Mechanics & Material Integrity
All existing approved mechanical assembly/extraction orders, physical gear ratios, and fade logic remain untouched [8, 9]. The pre-sequence drivetrain cascade is corrected purely through timing: planet gear rotation is held static until its owning planetary carrier physically separates, after which native scroll distance is reallocated generously to later stages (sun gear, friction clutch stack, and needle bearings). No post-processed depth-of-field, destructive cutaway clipping, or custom lighting systems are introduced; framing relies entirely on camera proximity, perspective projection [10, 11], and macro composition [12, 13].

---

### Concept 1: "Closer Axial Dolly Tracking" (Primary Recommendation)

* **Visual Thesis**: A high-impact macro perspective that dollies laterally alongside the drivetrain axis at an elevated side 3/4 angle, bringing interior CAD details close to the viewer while maintaining diagonal parallax [11, 12, 14].

```
                ELEVATED SIDE 3/4 DIAGONAL VECTOR
               abs(viewDirection . motionAxis) < 0.6
                                 \
                                  \   [Axial Motion Axis] --->
                                   v
        +-------------------+    [Stage 1 Carrier] ---> [Clutch Stack] ---> [LCD Screen]
        | DOM Caption Zone  |      (Macro Focus)          (Expanded Scroll)    (End Frame)
        +-------------------+
```

#### 4 Plain-Language Styleframes & Narrative Purpose
1. **Styleframe 1 — Housing Release & Occlusion Lead-In**:
   * *Visual*: Elevated side 3/4 angle on the assembled JGun torque wrench handle. The outer shell begins axial retraction toward the left frame edge [14, 15].
   * *Narrative Purpose*: Establish component identity and initiate the exploded sequence, using outer housing movement across the frame edge as a natural depth cue [16, 17].
2. **Styleframe 2 — Owning Carrier & Planet Synchrony**:
   * *Visual*: The Stage 1 planetary carrier body extracts along the shaft axis. Planet gears remain stationary until the carrier body clears the ring gear, then begin synchronized rotation [12].
   * *Narrative Purpose*: Correct the drivetrain cascade pacing by locking planet motion strictly to owning carrier emergence, respecting true assembly logic [9].
3. **Styleframe 3 — Sun Gear & Friction Clutch Stack Expansion**:
   * *Visual*: The camera dollies smoothly along the diagonal axis, tracking the sun gear, needle bearings, and friction clutch plates as they separate across an expanded scroll allocation [13, 14].
   * *Narrative Purpose*: Provide dedicated visual space for complex internal mechanical layers, letting precision gear tooth profiles fill 65%–85% of the viewport height [11, 18].
4. **Styleframe 4 — Mechanical Lock & LCD Readout Frame**:
   * *Visual*: The expanded axial stack settles into its final exploded layout while the camera pans smoothly to terminate on the illuminated digital LCD torque display [10, 19].
   * *Narrative Purpose*: Resolve the mechanical breakdown by bridging physical drivetrain engineering directly into the digital user interface [12].

#### Proposed Viewport Scroll Pacing (Creative Proposal)
* **0% – 15% Scroll**: Outer housing release and initial shell retraction.
* **15% – 45% Scroll**: Stage 1 planetary carrier extraction and planet gear engagement.
* **45% – 80% Scroll**: Sun gear, needle bearings, and friction clutch stack explosion (expanded native scroll allocation).
* **80% – 100% Scroll**: Terminal alignment and lock-in on the angled digital LCD readout.

#### Narrow Viewport Strategy (\\(390 \times 844\\))
Rather than scaling down the CAD model, increase camera pitch to \\(\sim 45^\circ\\) to re-orient the diagonal explosion line vertically across the tall screen aspect ratio [20, 21]. CAD geometry maintains a 65%–80% viewport width fill, while DOM captions occupy dedicated top and bottom layout zones [22].

---

### Concept 2: "Helical Orbital Arc Sweep" (Alternative)

* **Visual Thesis**: A continuous, single-direction helical sweep around the expanding JGun assembly, combining steady orbital arc rotation with axial translation along a single \\(C^1\\)-smooth parametric curve [23-25].

#### 4 Plain-Language Styleframes & Narrative Purpose
1. **Styleframe 1 — Signed Orbit Initiation**:
   * *Visual*: Elevated side 3/4 view framing the torque wrench housing as a signed clockwise orbit begins [25].
   * *Narrative Purpose*: Introduce overall tool volume and establish a single, non-reversing rotational direction before parts separate [16, 26].
2. **Styleframe 2 — Side-Profile Carrier Reveal**:
   * *Visual*: Camera orbits around the side profile as the Stage 1 carrier extracts, capturing gear teeth profiles against ambient reflections [12, 27].
   * *Narrative Purpose*: Emphasize gear tooth meshing and rotational symmetry from a dynamic side profile [13].
3. **Styleframe 3 — Sweeping Clutch & Bearing Flare**:
   * *Visual*: The helical path sweeps past the friction clutch plates and needle bearings as they explode along the central shaft [14].
   * *Narrative Purpose*: Highlight precision surface finishes and component stacking through continuous angular perspective changes [27, 28].
4. **Styleframe 4 — Terminal Arc into LCD Readout**:
   * *Visual*: The orbital arc eases into a stationary hero position centered on the angled digital LCD readout [12, 19].
   * *Narrative Purpose*: Conclude the continuous orbital sweep on a clear, readable presentation pose [17, 18].

#### Proposed Viewport Scroll Pacing (Creative Proposal)
* **0% – 20% Scroll**: Housing release and orbit initiation.
* **20% – 45% Scroll**: Stage 1 carrier extraction and gear engagement.
* **45% – 85% Scroll**: Stage 2 sun gear, bearing, and friction clutch stack separation (extended allocation).
* **85% – 100% Scroll**: Arc sweep deceleration and terminal lock on LCD readout.

---

### Cheap Visual Preview & Approval Package

To allow owner review and approval prior to full WebGL implementation or rendering [29, 30]:
1. **4 Static CAD Key Stills**: High-resolution viewport captures representing Styleframes 1 through 4 (initial assembly, carrier emergence, clutch stack expansion, and final LCD frame) [29, 30].
2. **Short Scroll Animatic Clip**: A 5-second 60fps WebM/MP4 video or interactive Figma scroll prototype demonstrating camera position \\(\mathbf{P}(t)\\) smoothly progressing over \\(t \in [1]\\), verifying framing, diagonal parallax, caption clearance, and the \\(\text{abs}(\mathbf{v}_{\text{view}} \cdot \mathbf{v}_{\text{motion}}) < 0.6\\) vector constraint [29, 31, 32].

---

### Recommendation & Trade-Off Analysis

* **Recommended Concept**: **Concept 1 ("Closer Axial Dolly Tracking")**.
* **Why it Wins**: Concept 1 directly resolves the "small distant strip" issue by keeping the camera close to the mechanical axis (65%–85% viewport fill) while strictly enforcing side 3/4 diagonal depth (\\(\text{abs}(\mathbf{v}_{\text{view}} \cdot \mathbf{v}_{\text{motion}}) < 0.6\\)) [11, 14]. It delivers a macro portfolio presentation without introducing complex rotational motion across adjoining stages [12].
* **Main Trade-Off**: Because the CAD geometry fills a large portion of the frame, active DOM caption overlays must be strictly confined to dedicated side or top/bottom layout zones to prevent text from overlapping moving mechanical components [22].

---

### Distinction: Source-Backed Cinematography vs. Creative Inferences

| Concept Element | Notebook Source Grounding | Classification |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Perspective Projection vs. Orthographic** | Perspective camera provides spatial depth, close-up zoom capability, and first-person immersion over flat top-down views [10, 11]. | **Source-Backed Principle** |
| **Closed-Form Progress Function \\(t \in [1]\\)** | Binding camera and scene evaluation directly to normalized animation progress (`animationPhase` from 0 to 1) [2-7]. | **Source-Backed Principle** |
| **Spline Path Continuity** | Parametric 3D splines (`CatmullRomCurve3`) ensure smooth continuous camera positioning [3, 23, 24]. | **Source-Backed Principle** |
| **Shot Framing & Macro Detail** | Close-up shots isolate technical details and form, medium/establishing shots set spatial context [11-13, 15, 18]. | **Source-Backed Principle** |
| **Engineering CAD Accuracy** | Utilizing engineering CAD models directly in CGI preserves exact physical part identity [8, 9, 28]. | **Source-Backed Principle** |
| **Animatic & Styleframe Pre-production** | Approving visual storyboards and animatics prior to production rendering [29, 30]. | **Source-Backed Principle** |
| **Vector Dot Product Constraint \\(\text{abs}(\mathbf{v} \cdot \mathbf{m}) < 0.6\\)** | Specific mathematical threshold chosen to enforce side 3/4 framing and eliminate boresight viewing down the shaft. | **Project-Specific Inference** |
| **Viewport Scroll Allocation (%)** | Specific percentages of scroll distance assigned to planetary carriers vs. clutch stack. | **Project-Specific Inference** |
| **Mobile Aspect Pitch Adjustment (\\(45^\circ\\))** | Strategy of pitching camera to re-orient diagonal explosion line on tall screen aspect ratios (\\(390 \times 844\\)). | **Project-Specific Inference** |
| **LCD Readout Terminal Destination** | Choosing the illuminated digital LCD torque readout as the final sequence destination frame. | **Project-Specific Inference** |

*(Note: These visual concepts represent creative design proposals grounded in source principles and have not yet undergone WebGL code execution or physical render verification.)*
